questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Little did the shareholders know that the CEO planned to resign.
Little the shareholders knew that the CEO planned to resign.
Little did the shareholders knew that the CEO planned to resign.
Little the shareholders did know that the CEO planned to resign.
questions.explanation: 'Little' at the start triggers inversion with 'did': 'Little did the shareholders know...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The board recommended that the budget be revised immediately.
The board recommended that the budget is revised immediately.
The board recommended that the budget will be revised immediately.
The board recommended that the budget being revised immediately.
questions.explanation: After 'recommend that', formal English uses the subjunctive: 'the budget be revised.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: But for the timely intervention of the regulator, the bank would have collapsed.
But for the timely intervention of the regulator, the bank collapsed.
But the timely intervention of the regulator, the bank would have collapsed.
But for the timely intervention of the regulator, the bank will have collapsed.
questions.explanation: 'But for' means 'if it were not for': 'But for the intervention, the bank would have collapsed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Sales increased, albeit at a slower pace than forecast.
Sales increased, albeit that at a slower pace than forecast.
Sales increased albeit for a slower pace than forecast.
Sales increased, albeit it a slower pace than forecast.
questions.explanation: 'Albeit' can be followed directly by a prepositional phrase: 'albeit at a slower pace.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It was the supply chain disruption that ultimately drove prices up.
It was the supply chain disruption which ultimately drove prices up who.
It the supply chain disruption was that ultimately drove prices up.
It was the supply chain disruption whom ultimately drove prices up.
questions.explanation: Cleft sentences with a non-personal subject use 'It was [thing] that...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The economist contends that inflation will ease by next quarter.
The economist contends to that inflation will ease by next quarter.
The economist contends inflation will easing by next quarter.
The economist is contend that inflation will ease by next quarter.
questions.explanation: 'Contend' is followed by 'that + clause': 'contends that inflation will ease.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Having secured new funding, the startup expanded its operations abroad.
Having secure new funding, the startup expanded its operations abroad.
Have secured new funding, the startup expanded its operations abroad.
Having secured new funding, the startup expanding its operations abroad.
questions.explanation: 'Having + past participle' shows a completed prior action: 'Having secured new funding, the startup expanded...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A number of clients has raised concerns about the new pricing model.
A number of clients have raised concerns about the new pricing model.
The number of clients have raised concerns about the new pricing model.
A number of clients raising concerns about the new pricing model.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb: 'a number of clients have raised concerns.' ('The number of' would take a singular verb.)

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The firm should have diversified its portfolio before the downturn.
The firm should diversified its portfolio before the downturn.
The firm should have diversify its portfolio before the downturn.
The firm should have diversifying its portfolio before the downturn.
questions.explanation: 'Should have + past participle' expresses a missed obligation: 'should have diversified its portfolio.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Neither the CFO nor the auditors were aware of the discrepancy.
Neither the CFO or the auditors were aware of the discrepancy.
Neither the CFO nor the auditors was aware of the discrepancy.
Neither the CFO nor did the auditors aware of the discrepancy.
questions.explanation: 'Neither...nor' pairs with 'nor', and the verb agrees with the nearer subject: 'Neither the CFO nor the auditors were aware.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The merger will presumably be finalized before the end of the fiscal year.
The merger will presumable be finalized before the end of the fiscal year.
The merger presumably will be finalized that before the end of the fiscal year.
The merger will be presumably finalized it before the end of the fiscal year.
questions.explanation: 'Presumably' hedges a claim and typically sits after the modal: 'will presumably be finalized.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company adopted a policy whereby employees can work remotely two days a week.
The company adopted a policy where employees can work remotely two days a week by.
The company adopted a policy by which whereby employees can work remotely.
The company adopted a policy whereby that employees can work remotely.
questions.explanation: 'Whereby' introduces a formal relative clause meaning 'by which': 'a policy whereby employees can work remotely.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Such was the demand for the product that stock sold out within hours.
Such the demand for the product was that stock sold out within hours.
Such was the demand for the product stock sold out within hours.
Such was that the demand for the product stock sold out within hours.
questions.explanation: Fronting 'such + be' triggers inversion: 'Such was the demand... that stock sold out.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The implementation of the new software delayed the entire rollout.
The implement of the new software delayed the entire rollout.
The implementation of the new software delay the entire rollout.
The implementing the new software delayed the entire rollout.
questions.explanation: Formal writing nominalizes verbs: 'implement' becomes 'the implementation of...'

questions.topic: Passive with modal perfect (might have been)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The contract might have been signed sooner had both parties been more flexible.
The contract might been signed sooner had both parties been more flexible.
The contract might have signed sooner had both parties been more flexible.
The contract might have being signed sooner had both parties been more flexible.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive: modal + have been + past participle: 'might have been signed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: One department wanted more staff; another, more equipment.
One department wanted more staff; another wanted, more equipment.
One department wanted more staff; another is more equipment.
One department wanted more staff; another wants more equipment already.
questions.explanation: Ellipsis omits the repeated verb after a semicolon: 'another, more equipment' (= another wanted more equipment).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Demand for raw materials surged. Consequently, prices rose sharply.
Demand for raw materials surged, consequently prices rose sharply.
Demand for raw materials surged. Consequently prices rose sharply.
Demand for raw materials surged consequently, prices rose sharply.
questions.explanation: 'Consequently' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Despite the economic slowdown, the retailer reported record profits.
Despite of the economic slowdown, the retailer reported record profits.
Despite the economic slowdown, but the retailer reported record profits.
The economic slowdown despite of, the retailer reported record profits.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is followed directly by a noun phrase, with no 'of': 'Despite the slowdown...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email proposing a business partnership?
options: Hey, wanna team up on something big?
I am writing to propose a potential partnership that could benefit both our organizations.
So I had this idea about us working together lol.
Just checking if you'd be into partnering up.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to propose a potential partnership...' is a standard formal opening for business correspondence.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a billing error?
options: I am writing to raise a concern regarding a discrepancy in our most recent invoice.
Your billing is wrong and I'm not happy about it.
There's been a mistake with the invoice, fix it please.
I am writing to raise a concern regarding a discrepancy in our most recent invoice, thanks.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use precise, measured language such as 'I am writing to raise a concern regarding...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The firm decided to scale back its expansion plans amid rising costs.
The firm decided to scale its expansion plans back of amid rising costs.
The firm decided to scale back of its expansion plans amid rising costs.
The firm decided to scale the expansion plans of back amid rising costs.
questions.explanation: 'Scale back' means 'to reduce': 'scale back its expansion plans.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The deal got finalized just before the deadline.
The deal got finalize just before the deadline.
The deal got finalizing just before the deadline.
The deal was got finalized just before the deadline.
questions.explanation: get + past participle: 'the deal got finalized just before the deadline.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: That said, the long-term outlook for the sector remains positive.
That saying, the long-term outlook for the sector remains positive.
That says, the long-term outlook for the sector remains positive.
That said that, the long-term outlook for the sector remains positive.
questions.explanation: 'That said' is a fixed absolute participle phrase meaning 'despite that.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The firm restructured its debt with a view to improving cash flow.
The firm restructured its debt with a view of improving cash flow.
The firm restructured its debt with view to improving cash flow.
The firm restructured its debt with a view to improve cash flow.
questions.explanation: 'With a view to' is followed by a gerund: 'with a view to improving cash flow.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The two firms struck a deal after months of negotiation.
The two firms hit a deal after months of negotiation.
The two firms made a deal strike after months of negotiation.
The two firms struck of a deal after months of negotiation.
questions.explanation: 'Strike a deal' is a fixed collocation: 'the two firms struck a deal.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The regulator has repeatedly warned against reckless lending.
The regulator has warned repeatedly against reckless lending it.
Repeatedly the regulator has warned against reckless lending.
The regulator repeatedly has warned against reckless lending.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency typically follow the auxiliary verb: 'has repeatedly warned.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The proposal is underfunded. Moreover, it lacks a clear timeline.
The proposal is underfunded, moreover it lacks a clear timeline.
The proposal is underfunded. Moreover it lacks a clear timeline.
The proposal is underfunded moreover, it lacks a clear timeline.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: The committee would hardly reject such a profitable proposal, would it?
The committee would hardly reject such a profitable proposal, wouldn't it?
The committee would hardly reject such a profitable proposal, doesn't it?
The committee would hardly reject such a profitable proposal, does it?
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' makes the statement effectively negative, so the tag is positive: 'would hardly reject..., would it?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The negotiations were not entirely unsuccessful.
The negotiations were not all unsuccessful entirely.
The negotiations not were entirely unsuccessful.
The negotiations were entirely not unsuccessful.
questions.explanation: Formal understatement places 'not' before the adverb: 'were not entirely unsuccessful.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Should the market conditions worsen, the fund will reassess its strategy.
Should the market conditions worsen, the fund would reassessed its strategy.
Should market conditions worsening, the fund will reassess its strategy.
Should the market conditions worsen, the fund reassess will its strategy.
questions.explanation: 'Should + subject + base verb' is an inverted conditional meaning 'if...should': 'Should the market worsen, the fund will reassess.'
